full_text:
When it comes to predicting fantasy football outcomes, the list of variables is endless: coaching schemes, defensive matchups, game script, weather, and more. But while team or coaching tendencies are often the optimal starting point, QBs have the final say in who earns a target. Put late-career __Drew Brees__ in Sean McVay’s offense, and I’d bet good money __Kyren Williams__ gets peppered with targets like he’s __Alvin Kamara__. Schemes matter, but QB preferences can reshape how those schemes play out.

With this in mind, I will dive into QB positional target tendencies for all potential 2026 starting quarterbacks over a three-year sample size (2023-2025). Using this data, we can dial in on the QBs who target RBs, TEs, WRs, and the slot or outside at the highest/lowest rates and attempt to separate signal from noise to identify the most valuable trends heading into 2025.

Two important points before we get started: this data will be heavily skewed by sample size and a QB’s surrounding cast. Certain QBs (__Malik Willis__) have thrown very few passes, and thus, their target tendencies are much more likely to be noise than, say, __Jared Goff__’s.

Regarding the supporting cast, it should go without saying that if __Trey McBride__ is on your team, you are going to target TEs more because he’s among the best pass catchers in the NFL. I’ll do my best to acknowledge these factors in the analysis below.

Scroll to the bottom for a full chart of targets and percentages.

### __Running Backs__

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/a324be1682a66ac3bf9e467da89fdfd4cf21f125/2aa0ab630f2733d1edf8d9a259bc15db32ac7599)

+ One of the most consistent trends we see in this data is that older QBs target RBs at higher rates to avoid taking hits. There is no better example of that than __Aaron Rodgers__’ 22.1% RB target rate. Last season, __Kenneth Gainwell__ (0.41) and __Jaylen Warren__ (0.39) both ranked among the top 7 (of 59 qualifiers) in XFP/RR. A route from either Warren or Gainwell was worth more (by XFP/RR and FP/RR) than a route from Bijan Robinson, Chase Brown, or Ashton Jeanty. The receiving floor for Warren — and new addition __Rico Dowdle__ — is massive in an offense with a 42-year-old QB.

+ There is a tangible RB target gap between __Shedeur Sanders__ (25.5%) and __Deshaun Watson__ (18.0%), which is notable for __Quinshon Judkins__ and (particularly) __Dylan Sampson__ drafters. Ryan Heath noted that Todd Monken offenses have historically had [distinct and separate](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact#/) rushing and receiving roles in the backfield. Sampson (2.01 YPRR) easily beat Judkins (1.17) in receiving efficiency last year, and the Browns are implied for [roughly 6 wins](https://sportsbook.draftkings.com/leagues/football/nfl?category=futures&subcategory=wins&nav_1=regular-season-wins) by DraftKings this season, so volume shouldn’t be an issue. This is a best ball only take, but I want exposure to Sampson relative to where he’s being drafted on DraftKings (ADP: 171.9), particularly if Sanders ends up as the Browns starter.
+ __Bo Nix__ (20.4% RB target rate) just missed the top-5 by RB target rate, but by raw RB targets per game, Nix (7.1) actually ranks behind only __Tua Tagovailoa__ (7.8) over the last three seasons. The Broncos' infuriating RB rotation prevents this from translating into a clean fantasy take, but I do view __JK Dobbins__ (RB35 ADP) as a *slightly* better pick than __RJ Harvey__ (RB31) to beat ADP. Dobbins is [healthy](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49111942/jk-dobbins-priority-re-signing-denver-broncos-stay-healthy-help-rushing-attack), just [signed](https://x.com/spotrac/status/2032448569370648768?lang=en) a two-year extension, plays for the [best offensive line in football](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-offensive-line-rankings), and was an outright better rusher than Harvey (5.1 YPC to 3.7) while earning 49% of backfield XFP in his 10 games with Harvey.
+ __Malik Willis__ logs a league-low 10.8% RB target rate over the last three seasons, but I’m not worried about __De’Von Achane__’s receiving workload in 2026. Just 94 attempts from Willis make this a highly noisy sample of throws, and 86% of those throws were either designed or first-read targets. Sure, Willis is a [Konami Code QB](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2025/statistically-significant-scrambles-and-qb-runs#/), but he’s also a QB who won’t stray from the dictated throw of a particular play. Who do we think the Dolphins will scheme targets for? Malik Washington? Jalen Tolbert? Tutu Atwell? My money is on Achane continuing his target dominance despite Willis's historical tendencies. But, ultimately, I wouldn’t blame anyone who was scared off by Bobby Slowik [calling plays](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact#/).
+ Of course, it’s worth noting that players like __Brock Purdy__, __Tua Tagovailoa__, and __Jared Goff__ (who finished 6th in our sample with a 20.5% RB target rate) are all playing with elite receiving RBs, and with coaches who are happy to scheme up targets for those RBs. Tagovailoa is particularly spoiled in this regard, going from __De’Von Achane__ to __Bijan Robinson__ (two of the top-3 RBs by first-read target share over the last three seasons).

### __Slot Pass Catchers__

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/a324be1682a66ac3bf9e467da89fdfd4cf21f125/39ec1c02b9876c81f7719217893d30d2f68181ef)

+ __Jaxson Dart__’s league-leading slot target rate stands out against his league-average positional target rates. Of course, we can attribute this in part to __Malik Nabers'__ injury and to __Wan’Dale Robinson__ (68% slot rate) racking up 132 targets in Nabers' absence. But with Robinson in Tennessee and Nabers still on the mend, I do wonder if we are underrating __Isaiah Likely__ as a slot pass catcher. Among the 64 TEs to run at least 100 slot routes over the last three seasons, Likely ranks 14th in FP/RR (0.37) and 14th in YPRR (1.65). In fact, Likely’s 1.65 YPRR from the slot over that span is only slightly worse than Nabers (1.85) and notably better than teammates __Calvin Austin__ (1.02) and __Darius Slayton__ (0.96). If Dart’s slot target rate is at all sticky (and if OC __Matt Nagy__ really is a [TE whisperer](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact#/)), then Likely could pop from a volume perspective in a big way this season.

+ __Cam Ward__ had an affinity for targeting the slot when his slot WRs were Tyler Lockett and Chimere Dike, and I want to bet on another productive season from __Wan’Dale Robinson__ now that he’s in Tennessee. Robinson has led all players since 2023 in first-read target share from the slot (19.1%), and he’s reunited with OC __Brian Daboll__ (who just coached Robinson to a WR17 finish). I want to be ahead of the market on Robinson, who finished 2025 with the 7th-most games with double-digit targets (7), particularly in PPR formats.

 Leaders in 1st read target share from the slot since 2023 (via @FantasyPtsData ): Wan'Dale Robinson* - 19.1% Amon-Ra St. Brown - 18.6% Cooper Kupp - 17.2% Josh Downs - 16.5% Ladd McConkey - 16.2% *Paired with a QB who ranks top-5 in slot target rate since 2023 — Jake Tribbey (@JakeTribbey) July 9, 2026 

+ __Trevor Lawrence__’s target data and HC __Liam Coen__’s [love of slot pass catchers](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2072796352707268772?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2072796352707268772%7Ctwgr%5E5d00d551673d03a2eb7527115e660dfa41e339b6%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fantasypoints.com%2Fnfl%2Farticles%2Fseason%2F2026%2Fnew-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact%2F) bolster the argument that __Travis Hunter__ is a strong late-round best ball pick. Sure, Hunter will be a [part-time player](https://x.com/DhananiZain/status/2075007429851431395) in Week 1, but he has a relatively clean path to a full-time role if any of __Jakobi Meyers__, __Brian Thomas__, or __Parker Washington__ get hurt. Additional WR depth is [nonexistent](https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/depth/_/name/jax), and Hunter led the team in designed target rate (18%) and finished tied for 2nd (with Brenton Strange) in TPRR (0.21) in 2025. I want to bet on a [generational talent](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/2025/profiles/rookie/db#/) on a [great offense](https://x.com/JakeTribbey/status/2077794246526918686?s=20) who was fed designed targets whenever he was on the field last year (even if it conflicts with our best ball rankings).

### __Wide Pass Catchers__

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/a324be1682a66ac3bf9e467da89fdfd4cf21f125/8e78e94ba5e6da7f7d1caec1bd58901d84ae0299)

+ There is no bigger gap in teammate target rates for pass catchers lined up out wide than __Shedeur Sanders__ (29.7%) and __Deshaun Watson__ (42.9%). Watson starting over Sanders would most clearly benefit __Jerry Jeudy__ (ADP: 183.1), who has run 64% of his routes from out wide over the last three seasons. New playcaller and HC __Todd Monken__ has led all coaches over the last five years in ANY/A (7.6) and yards per play (6.2). Meanwhile, Jeudy has earned 6.6 targets per game (~WR30) and 11.5 XFP/G (~WR32) over the last three seasons, yet he’s being drafted as the WR72 on DraftKings. There is added receiving competition this year, and Jeudy isn’t a league-winner, but I do view him as a clear ADP-beater, and our [best ball rankings](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/rankings/best-ball#draftkings/) back that up.

+ __Kyler Murray__ (30.7%) has the 2nd-lowest outside target rate in our sample, which directly conflicts with __Kevin O’Connell__’s 43.5% outside target rate since 2023 (16th of 58 playcallers). The good news for O’Connell is that Murray (+0.12 EPA/DB) has been dramatically more efficient targeting outside pass catchers than __JJ McCarthy__ (-0.04 EPA/DB). The bad news? Murray still ranks 49th of 55 QBs over the last three seasons in catchable target rate to players lined up outside (71.8%), and his 0.12 EPA/DB ranks 45th. Murray is an upgrade over McCarthy, but I’m not banking on elite outside efficiency from __Justin Jefferson__ or __Jordan Addison__ this season. If I had to fully fade any Round 1 player, it would be Jefferson – who showed a disastrous floor (8.7 FPG) in his final eight games in 2025.
+ I expect __Jalen Hurts__' [passing tendencies](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact#/) to be a bit more balanced in 2026, but we can still build a bull case for __Dontayvion Wicks__ based around Hurts’ top-5 outside target rate. Hurts has ranked no lower than 11th among QBs with at least 100 pass attempts in outside target rate over each of the last three seasons, despite three different play callers over that stretch. AJ Brown’s presence obviously influenced this, but Wicks has a clear path to starting on the outside, and he bests __DeVonta Smith__ in TPRR (0.24 to 0.23) from out wide over the last three seasons. By 1D/RR on the outside (since 2023), Wicks (0.095) has been better than Tee Higgins (0.09), Jameson Williams (0.093), and Christian Watson (0.087). OC __Sean Mannion__ wanted to bring Wicks to Philadelphia, so why shouldn’t we bring Wicks onto our best ball teams at a meager WR75 ADP?

### __Tight Ends__

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/a324be1682a66ac3bf9e467da89fdfd4cf21f125/ae72745fdc511234a8045385ec1fb3ae819ce2b6)

+ __Trey McBride__ and __Travis Kelce__ are the perfect examples of QB tendencies taking a back seat to raw pass-catcher skill. I won’t spend much time on either player, but it’s noteworthy that __Harold Fannin__ pushed the Browns' TE target rate from 26% in 2024 (9th-most) to 33% in 2025 (2nd-most). Among the 24 TEs to run at least 200 routes as a rookie since 2021, Fannin ranks top-5 in FP/RR (0.45), XFP/RR (0.45), first-read target share (22.3%), and YPRR (1.81). The coaching change to __Todd Monken__ is a neutral-at-worst change for Fannin; Monken’s TEs have averaged more XFP/G (15.5) over the last five years than Kevin Stefanski's TEs (15.0). Fannin (like most TEs this year) is a quality pick at cost.

+ __Tua Tagovailoa__ owns one of the lowest TE target rates in the NFL, yet __Darren Waller__ and __Jonnu Smith__ have combined for 9 games of at least 17.0 fantasy points since 2024 (Brock Bowers has 7 such games over that timespan). An outlierish amount of TE spike weeks can only be explained by playcaller __Mike McDaniel__. Over the last two seasons, McDaniel’s TEs are responsible for the 4th-most games of 17-plus fantasy points, despite Miami ranking 10th in TE target share over that stretch. Is there a more exciting new pairing at the position than McDaniel and __Oronde Gadsden__? Ryan Heath lays out a great McDaniel-based bull case [here](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact#/), but the TL;DR is that I’m taking as much Gadsden as I can stomach at a TE18 ADP.
+ __Juwan Johnson__ averaged 57.4 receiving YPG, 1.94 YPRR, and 11.4 FPG in his 10 full games with __Tyler Shough__ in 2025. Over the full season, those numbers would have ranked 3rd-best, 8th-best, and 9th-best among TEs. I’m happy to take Johnson at a TE21 ADP; despite added target competition, New Orleans is [implied](https://establishtherun.com/nfl-average-implied-team-totals-2026/) for 21.5 PPG this season, a +19% increase on the 18.0 PPG they averaged in 2025.

### __Notable Backup Tendencies__

+ Don’t forget about the receiving upside of Kansas City RBs if __Justin Fields__ starts in Week 1; he breaks the standard Konami Code [mold](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2025/statistically-significant-scrambles-and-qb-runs#/) by targeting RBs at a 22.6% rate (with three different teams), while __Patrick Mahomes__ clocks in at just 16.3%.

+ __Tommy DeVito__’s 22.3% RB target rate is notably higher than __Drake Maye__’s 16.6%. Expect more backfield targets in New England if the Italian Stallion takes over due to a Maye injury.
+ __Mark Andrews__ averages more FPG (13.2) and targets per game (7.4) in __Tyler Huntley__’s 10 starts over the last five seasons than in his 63 games with __Lamar Jackson__ (12.3 FPG, 5.7 targets per game).
+ There is a notable drop-off in RB target rate between __Daniel Jones__ (15.0%) and __Anthony Richardson__ (9.7%). This is partially due to Richardson’s addiction to throwing deep – his 12.3 aDOT over the last two seasons is the highest of any QB with at least 200 pass attempts.
+ __Jarrett Stidham__ owns the highest RB target rate of the last five years (25.7%). This is notable, although it’s not an extreme difference relative to Broncos starter __Bo Nix__ (20.4%).
+ __Jameis Winston__ (10.2%) has one of the lowest RB target rates in our sample, while starter __Jaxson Dart__ (18.0%) is almost perfectly league-average.
+ __Tyson Bagent__ (23.9% RB target rate) is notably more eager to throw to the backfield than __Caleb Williams__ (14.4%).
+ __Jordan Love__ (19.0%) owns a bottom-7 TE target rate among potential 2026 starters, but backup __Tyrod Taylor__ (24.3%) would rank 11th-highest.
+ __Jake Browning__ has a lower aDOT (6.8) than __Baker Mayfield__ (8.1) over the last three seasons. Interestingly, this doesn’t show up much in Browning’s RB target rate (17.2%), but Browning’s TE target rate (23.3%) is much higher than Mayfield’s (16.6%).
+ Among QBs with at least 100 attempts over the last three seasons, no QB has a higher WR target rate than Seattle backup __Drew Lock__ (71%). For comparison, __Sam Darnold__ is at 63%.
